findings.failure_path: An agent follows the playbook's authoritative localization table instead of the condensed entrypoint. For a multi-component failure it is told to run the chain once and log actual entry/exit data plus received env/config, even when rerunning is unsafe or a boundary is unreachable; this can persist bodies, secrets, PII, or configuration values and provides no telemetry/partial-evidence fallback. The regression row similarly prescribes pathspec narrowing without requiring evidence that the paths contain the cause or retrying the full range after a false-negative restricted search.
findings.smallest_fix: Make both table recipes mirror the entrypoint: boundary-walk only when safely rerunnable and fully reachable, logging only allowlisted redacted metadata/config keys with telemetry or partial-evidence fallback; pathspec narrowing only when supported by evidence, followed by a full-range bisect if it finds no reproducing commit.

concern_results.conclusion: Failed. The entrypoint adds the required boundary-walk safety conditions and fallback, but the referenced Localization Playbook still instructs unconditional one-run logging of actual entry/exit data and env/config, creating a data-leak and unsafe-rerun bypass. Its commit-bisection recipe also omits the entrypoint's evidence precondition and full-range fallback. Prediction/falsifier fields are consistently separated, and the attribution file supplies URLs and excerpts for the newly listed sources.
